law: fs_per_weight_floor = 152.6252 * BPW (model-independent). token_ns_floor = active_weights * BPW/8 / 819e9. TPS ceiling = 1/token_ns_floor.

machine_reference.note: Use the measured control, not 819, when judging efficiency. Packed matvecs currently run ~2.5 GB/s.

q80.artifact: mixed-1p5-v1 PACKED, generation not yet proven
q80.TERMINAL: TG3/333 is REACHABLE at the current 1.44445 BPW with 3.82x headroom. Q80 has the most room of the three because MoE sparsity keeps active weights at 3.562 G.

dsv4f.TERMINAL: 50 and 100 TPS are workable at 1.5 BPW. TG3/333 is MARGINAL at 1.03x - it would demand ~97% of peak bandwidth, which is not credible. Comfortable TG3 needs <= 0.6173 BPW, i.e. sub-bit.

qwen38.TERMINAL: 50 TPS workable at 2.0 BPW (2.77x). 100 TPS is MARGINAL (1.39x) and needs BPW below 2.0. TG3/333 is PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE at 2.0 BPW (0.42x) and would require 0.3333 BPW. Its realistic terminal is the 100-139 tok/s band. That is fine - it is a developer unit, not a tournament contender.

sub_100_fs_threshold.applies_to: ALL THREE models identically, because the fs/weight floor is model-independent
sub_100_fs_threshold.note: Sub-100 fs/weight requires BPW < 0.6552 AND near-unity bandwidth efficiency. Both are mandatory.

bpw_for_comfortable_tg3.note: At 2.5x headroom. Q80's requirement is ABOVE its current BPW, so Q80 already qualifies.

THE_SINGLE_SHARED_BLOCKER: All three need the same fix. Every gate above assumes efficiency near 1.0. Measured efficiency is ~0.4% of the 560-647 GB/s control. Until packed matvec occupancy is solved, NONE of these ceilings are reachable and the differences between models are academic.
